items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: I always did love drums because I was born in the third ward and that was, a section for jazz probably because Lee Armstrong was from that ward. He was born and raised around there.

ctx.x: Okay, well we're interviewing Joe Watkins this March 24th, 1969. Just going from what you're about to say, Joe, about when you started music.

When I started, I started in 1920s. Well that was quite a few years after George Lewis and Paul Barbrain. Well I always did love drums because I was born in the third ward and that was, a section for jazz probably because Lee Armstrong was from that ward. He was born and raised around there. And I don't know about Joe Oliver because I always heard that Joe was not exactly from the Orlins. But it was him, Lee Armstrong, Funk Johnson, and you had Manuel Moneta. And, uh, was this other fella's name, uh, was a good…
What sort of date was this? Huh? What date was this about?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: the first ones I remember outside of Bunk Johnson when I was small, outside of him was Louis Armstrong when Louis was coming up around his teens.

ctx.x: And how many guys in the band? Do you remember the band that band? It was four then, at that time, I remember. What was your uncle playing?

He didn't even have no drum with him. He was playing Ghetto at that time. Uh-huh. He was taking up banjo in later years. That's when he went with Louis. He plays occasionally at, you know, like all weekends out there in California.

Well, guys like that, they aren't good enough to work. They only work with Louis Armstrong, Jelly Roll Morton, King Oliver, and all the rest of them. And yet today they're not working. Isn't that funny?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: Well it was Joe, it was Louis Armstrong, Kid Ory, Lorenzo Teo, Joe Lindsey.

ctx.x: Well, what about Joe Lindsey? How did he play and who did he play with? Do you remember much about that?

Well, Joe Lindsey was playing down on Claiborne between Quarntire and St. Louis. They had a dance hall there in them days. And he was playing with Kid Ory. Well Louis played down there for a while too, before you know, before he went out there on the boat. Well it was Joe, it was Louis Armstrong, Kid Ory, Lorenzo Teo, Joe Lindsey. I forgot who else he had with him. But they didn't have no piano. He had seven men. They wasn't using no piano. They was using a saxophone and banjo, clarinet, trumpet, trombone, drums,…
I met Joe Lindsey once in Chicago and then he came back here. I never met him here later, but I know he didn't play much in late years.
